_note: REACHED VIA PROBE, and deliberately: a guide exists only mid-drag, and
`calculateSnapping` derives it from sibling geometry read out of a real
canvas DOM — a fixture canvas would make the measurement a statement about
the fixture's rectangles, not about the guide. What the board actually
specifies is the LINE: colour, thickness, extent. So the REAL
SmartGuidesOverlay is mounted over the board's own seven line geometries,
board's own 464x180 cell coordinates. Every pixel measured is drawn by the
component from the same SnapLine shape the drag hands it; nothing is
hardcoded to look like a guide. All four scenarios are covered — centre
alignment, edge alignment, equal spacing and parent padding.
BOARD WON — the spacing red. The four spacing rects are filled
--color/error, which is #E02424; the overlay painted #FF4444. Note the
board CONTRADICTS ITSELF here: its own blurb (815:4610) reads 'Red
(#FF4444) spacing indicators', and that sentence is what the component was
built from. A tokenised fill in the DRAWING beats an untokenised number in
a CAPTION — the drawing is the design, the caption describes it — so the
four rects win. The magenta #FF00FF alignment guides and the 1px thickness
already matched.
CONTRAST — this change IMPROVED it, and it is still short. Measured on the
probe's bg-subtle cell (the board's own cell fill): the gap labels went
from #FF4444 on #F3F4F6 = 3.04:1 to #E02424 on #F3F4F6 = 4.29:1, against
a 4.5 floor. Two things about that number: it is BETTER than what shipped,
and it is not really the product's number — in the app these labels sit
over the CUSTOMER's canvas, whose background is theirs, not ours. Recorded
in the baseline as measured rather than argued away, and flagged: a label
chip (white pill behind the number) is the only thing that would make this
legible at every canvas colour, and that is a design decision.
NOT CONFORMED — the four label nodes (815:4634/4636/4644/4646). The board
sets them 10px Inter Medium; the overlay draws 11px/500. 10 is not a step
of the type scale, and `check-design-debt-ratchet`'s `offscale-font-size`
rule (which matches the literal `fontSize: 10`) is locked at ZERO over
src/editor — a 10 here fails the build. The colour and weight DID move
with the lines. Worth a founder ruling: the ratchet already excludes
CatalogCard, BrandPreview and TypographySection on the grounds that they
draw at a scale that is not chrome type, and this file carries the same
argument in its own header (`@lint-hex-policy: component-theme` — 'this
paints ON the customer's canvas, not chrome'). Adding it to that list is
a gate change, so it is reported, not taken.
NOT JOINED — the board's rectangles, cards and captions (815:4611 etc.).
They are the documentation sheet's own furniture: four 496x280 explainer
cards drawn to describe the guides, with sample elements in blue-100. No
product surface renders them.
